dedupe_keys.name: nvidia aerial omniverse digital twin aodt

description: The NVIDIA Aerial Omniverse Digital Twin (AODT) is a collection of frameworks and tools for building physically accurate digital twins of 5G and 6G wireless systems, from a single tower to a whole city. It combines GPU ray-traced radio propagation over realistic terrain and 3D objects with software-defined radio access network and user-equipment simulators, so that network behaviour, scheduling and AI-based RAN functions can be tested in a virtual copy of a real deployment. NVIDIA develops it as part of its AI Aerial portfolio for operators, vendors and researchers. The open-source repository provides the simulation client (C++ and Python libraries over gRPC for Linux, macOS and Windows), the Digital Twin worker run with Docker Compose, a 3D geospatial viewer and a development container; the complete software and releases come through the NVIDIA 6G Developer Program. Coverage: any area for which the user supplies terrain and building geometry, at the resolution of those scenes. Format and access: source on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 licence, free of charge, with full releases after free registration in the developer program; NVIDIA GPUs are needed. Caveats: heavy hardware requirements; city-scale scenes need detailed 3D data; the tool is new and changes quickly. Simulation uses: radio network digital twins, coverage and hazard exposure studies, capacity planning and resilience testing of mobile networks. Related records: builds on the same ray-tracing ideas as Sionna, and competes with Wireless InSite, Atoll and Planet for coverage prediction.
